The local critical-care pathway remains rural facility → Retrieval Services Queensland (RSQ) → Advanced Neonatal Transport Services North Queensland, with video added to—not replacing—the specialist consultation.\n\n'
    - '2. Local information indicates 4–5 video-supported episodes at Atherton to date and anticipated use of 10–15 consultations per site each year (30–45 across the three-site network). The installed cost is reported as $10,000 per installation; this should be verified against invoices and the component list.\n\n'
    - '3. The principal comparison is video-supported consultation versus telephone-supported consultation. Consultation occurs in both pathways. Potential value arises through: (a) avoiding a transfer that is not clinically required; (b) earlier or more precise procedures and stabilisation before a transfer that remains necessary; (c) improved specialist assessment, clinician confidence and communication with families; and (d) possible changes in survival or morbidity.\n\n'
    - '4. A randomised trial is unlikely to be feasible or appropriate for this low-volume emergency service. The recommended design is an annual-cohort decision model using the existing 4–5 episodes, routine historical activity, IHACPA admitted-care benchmarks, published teleneonatology evidence and explicitly reasoned assumptions. All assumptions will be classified as documented, externally informed or researcher-estimated.\n\n'
    - '5. The primary analysis will be a cost-consequence analysis from CHHHS, whole-health-system and societal perspectives, with a three- and five-year budget impact. It will report programme costs, transfers avoided, treatment/stabilisation consequences, family travel and separation, and the distribution of net costs. It will not equate NWAU revenue with marginal cash savings.\n\n'
    - '6. The model will use the 2026–27 National Efficient Price ($7,418 per NWAU) and AR-DRG version 12.0 neonatal weights to benchmark admitted resource use. Actual DRG/NWAU records should replace generic weights where available. Rural block-funding arrangements under the National Efficient Cost model will be described separately.\n\n'
    - '7. Public QAS reporting confirms substantial RSQ activity but does not publish a current neonatal road/rotary/fixed-wing split. The base case therefore uses a Queensland neonatal retrieval study (25 road, 9 rotary and 11 fixed-wing journeys) as a prior, with low-air and high-air scenarios. Asset and downstream hospital costs will be tested over broad ranges.\n\n'
    - '8. Deterministic scenarios will test no transfer effect, low/moderate/high effects, 10–15 consultations per site, alternative transport mixes and equipment configurations. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis will jointly vary utilisation, usual-care transfer probability, video effect, transport mode/cost, downstream hospital costs and programme costs. The transfer-effect distribution will cross the null so the analysis can represent no benefit or increased transfer.\n\n'
    - '9. An exploratory clinical extension will include death, survival without major morbidity and survival with major morbidity. This is important because preventing death can increase lifetime costs where additional survivors have significant morbidity. It will remain outside the primary result unless credible outcome parameters can be supported.\n\n'
    - '10. Published economic models support this structure. The earlier Queensland analysis found 5 avoided transfers among 19 consultations and a 5% break-even threshold, but used older technology and costs. Recent United States models used decision trees and Monte Carlo simulation and generally found tele-neonatology likely to be cost-saving, with substantial uncertainty. These estimates will inform ranges rather than be treated as local effects.\n\n'
    - '11. No exact off-the-shelf, medically integrated tablet-mounted PTZ system was verified. OBSBOT Tail Air is a plausible component because it supports 4K PTZ, tablet control, Wi-Fi/NDI, USB-C and PoE. It is not a clinically approved configuration. A tablet-integrated replacement for the current ad hoc setup should be prototyped and assessed by Biomedical Technology Services, eHealth Telehealth, cyber/privacy and end users.\n\n'
    - '12. Deliverables will be an editable economic model, executive briefing and presentation suitable for local, Queensland and national investment decisions, with a later prospective registry only if the value-of-information analysis indicates that further data collection could change the decision.'
